[India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India") hosted the [2010 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Commonwealth_Games "2010 Commonwealth Games") which were held in [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi") from 3 to 14 October 2010. India won 101 medals in total, including 38 Gold medals, enabling it to finish the Games at second position behind [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia"). For the first time in the history of the Games India won over 100 medals in total. For the first time in the history of the Games, India won a medal in [Gymnastics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics "Gymnastics"), where [Ashish Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashish_Kumar_(gymnast) "Ashish Kumar (gymnast)") won a Silver and a Bronze. And it was after a gap of 52 years that India won a Gold in Athletics when [Krishna Poonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia "Krishna Poonia") won Gold in [Women's discus throw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2010_Commonwealth_Games_%E2%80%93_Women's_discus_throw "Athletics at the 2010 Commonwealth Games – Women's discus throw") and when [Geeta Phogat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geeta_Phogat "Geeta Phogat") won India's first ever gold medal in women's wrestling.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_at_the_2010_Commonwealth_Games#cite_note-2)

[India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India") hosted the [2010 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Commonwealth_Games "2010 Commonwealth Games") which were held in [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi") from 3 to 14 October 2010. India won 101 medals in total, including 38 Gold medals, enabling it to finish the Games at second position behind [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia"). For the first time in the history of the Games India won over 100 medals in total. For the first time in the history of the Games, India won a medal in [Gymnastics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics "Gymnastics"), where [Ashish Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashish_Kumar_(gymnast) "Ashish Kumar (gymnast)") won a Silver and a Bronze. And it was after a gap of 52 years that India won a Gold in Athletics when [Krishna Poonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia "Krishna Poonia") won Gold in [Women's discus throw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2010_Commonwealth_Games_%E2%80%93_Women's_discus_throw "Athletics at the 2010 Commonwealth Games – Women's discus throw") and when [Geeta Phogat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geeta_Phogat "Geeta Phogat") won India's first ever gold medal in women's wrestling.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_at_the_2010_Commonwealth_Games#cite_note-2)

The **Arjuna Award**, officially known as **Arjuna Awards given for Outstanding Performance in Sports and Games**,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-Scheme-3) is the second-highest sporting honour of [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"), the highest being the Major Dhyan Chand [Khel Ratna Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khel_Ratna_Award "Khel Ratna Award"). The award is named after [Arjuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna "Arjuna"), one of the characters of the [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit")[epic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_epic_poetry "Indian epic poetry")_[Mahabharata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahabharata "Mahabharata")_ of [ancient India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_India "History of India").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-4) In [Hinduism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism "Hinduism"), he has been seen as a symbol of hard work, dedication and concentration.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-5) It is awarded annually by the [Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Youth_Affairs_and_Sports "Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports"). Before the introduction of the [Major Dhyan Chand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhyan_Chand "Dhyan Chand")[Khel Ratna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khel_Ratna_Award "Khel Ratna Award") in 1991–1992, the Arjuna award was the highest sporting honour of India.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-EverestNews-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-7) The nominations for the award are received from all government-recognised national sports federations, the [Indian Olympic Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Olympic_Association "Indian Olympic Association"), the [Sports Authority of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Authority_of_India "Sports Authority of India") (SAI), the Sports Promotion and Control Boards, the state and the union territory governments and the Major Dhyan Chandra Khel Ratna, Arjuna, [Dhyan Chand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhyan_Chand_Award "Dhyan Chand Award") and [Dronacharya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dronacharya_Award "Dronacharya Award") awardees of the previous years. The recipients are selected by a committee constituted by the Ministry and are honoured for their "good performance in the field of sports over a period of four years" at the international level and for having shown "qualities of leadership, sportsmanship and a sense of discipline." As of 2020[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arjuna_Award&action=edit), the award comprises "a [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze")[statuette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statuette "Statuette") of Arjuna, certificate, ceremonial dress, and a cash prize of ₹15 lakh (US$16,000)."[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-a-8)

Instituted in 1961 to honour the outstanding sportspersons of the country,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-9) the award over the years has undergone a number of expansions, reviews and rationalizations. The award was expanded to include all the recognised sporting disciplines in 1977, introduced indigenous games and physically handicapped categories in 1995 and introduced a lifetime contribution category in 1995 leading to creation of a separate [Dhyan Chand Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhyan_Chand_Award "Dhyan Chand Award") in 2002.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-11) The latest revision in 2018 stipulates that the award is given only to the disciplines included in the events like [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games"), [Paralympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paralympic_Games "Paralympic Games"), [Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Games "Asian Games"), [Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Games "Commonwealth Games"), [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_championship "World championship") and [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_cup_competition "World cup competition") along with [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket"), indigenous games, and [Parasports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disabled_sports "Disabled sports"). It also recommends giving only fifteen awards in a year, relaxing in case of excellent performance in major [multi-sport events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-sport_event "Multi-sport event"), team sports, across gender and giving away of at least one award in the physically challenged category.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-Scheme-3)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arjuna_Award&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Since the year 2001, the award is given only in disciplines falling under the following categories:

*   Olympic Games / Asian Games / Commonwealth Games / World Cup / World Championship Disciplines and Cricket
*   Indigenous Games
*   Sports for the Physically Challenged

The **Arjuna Award**, officially known as **Arjuna Awards given for Outstanding Performance in Sports and Games**,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-Scheme-3) is the second-highest sporting honour of [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"), the highest being the Major Dhyan Chand [Khel Ratna Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khel_Ratna_Award "Khel Ratna Award"). The award is named after [Arjuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna "Arjuna"), one of the characters of the [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit")[epic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_epic_poetry "Indian epic poetry")_[Mahabharata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahabharata "Mahabharata")_ of [ancient India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_India "History of India").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-4) In [Hinduism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism "Hinduism"), he has been seen as a symbol of hard work, dedication and concentration.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-5) It is awarded annually by the [Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Youth_Affairs_and_Sports "Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports"). Before the introduction of the [Major Dhyan Chand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhyan_Chand "Dhyan Chand")[Khel Ratna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khel_Ratna_Award "Khel Ratna Award") in 1991–1992, the Arjuna award was the highest sporting honour of India.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-EverestNews-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-7) The nominations for the award are received from all government-recognised national sports federations, the [Indian Olympic Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Olympic_Association "Indian Olympic Association"), the [Sports Authority of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Authority_of_India "Sports Authority of India") (SAI), the Sports Promotion and Control Boards, the state and the union territory governments and the Major Dhyan Chandra Khel Ratna, Arjuna, [Dhyan Chand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhyan_Chand_Award "Dhyan Chand Award") and [Dronacharya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dronacharya_Award "Dronacharya Award") awardees of the previous years. The recipients are selected by a committee constituted by the Ministry and are honoured for their "good performance in the field of sports over a period of four years" at the international level and for having shown "qualities of leadership, sportsmanship and a sense of discipline." As of 2020[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arjuna_Award&action=edit), the award comprises "a [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze")[statuette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statuette "Statuette") of Arjuna, certificate, ceremonial dress, and a cash prize of ₹15 lakh (US$16,000)."[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-a-8)

Instituted in 1961 to honour the outstanding sportspersons of the country,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-9) the award over the years has undergone a number of expansions, reviews and rationalizations. The award was expanded to include all the recognised sporting disciplines in 1977, introduced indigenous games and physically handicapped categories in 1995 and introduced a lifetime contribution category in 1995 leading to creation of a separate [Dhyan Chand Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhyan_Chand_Award "Dhyan Chand Award") in 2002.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-11) The latest revision in 2018 stipulates that the award is given only to the disciplines included in the events like [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games"), [Paralympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paralympic_Games "Paralympic Games"), [Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Games "Asian Games"), [Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Games "Commonwealth Games"), [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_championship "World championship") and [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_cup_competition "World cup competition") along with [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket"), indigenous games, and [Parasports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disabled_sports "Disabled sports"). It also recommends giving only fifteen awards in a year, relaxing in case of excellent performance in major [multi-sport events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-sport_event "Multi-sport event"), team sports, across gender and giving away of at least one award in the physically challenged category.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna_Award#cite_note-Scheme-3)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arjuna_Award&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Since the year 2001, the award is given only in disciplines falling under the following categories:

*   Olympic Games / Asian Games / Commonwealth Games / World Cup / World Championship Disciplines and Cricket
*   Indigenous Games
*   Sports for the Physically Challenged

The Arjuna Award, officially known as the Arjuna Awards for Outstanding Performance in Sports and Games,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-Scheme-1) is the sports honour of the [Republic of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"). It is awarded annually by the [Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Youth_Affairs_and_Sports "Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports"). Before the introduction of the [Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_Dhyan_Chand_Khel_Ratna "Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna") in 1991–1992, the Arjuna award was the highest sporting honour of India.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-EverestNews-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-3)As of 2020[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)&action=edit), the award comprises "a [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze")[statuette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statuette "Statuette") of Arjuna, certificate, ceremonial dress, and a cash prize of ₹15 lakh (US$16,000)."[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-a-4)

## Name

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Name")]

The award is named after [Arjuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna "Arjuna"), a character from the [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit") epic _[Mahabharata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahabharata "Mahabharata")_ of [ancient India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_India "History of India"). He is one of the [Pandavas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandavas "Pandavas"), depicted as a skilled [archer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archery "Archery") winning the hand of [Draupadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draupadi "Draupadi") in marriage. In the [Kurukshetra War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurukshetra_War "Kurukshetra War"), Lord [Krishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna "Krishna") becomes his charioteer teaching him the sacred knowledge of [Gita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhagavad_Gita "Bhagavad Gita").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-5) In [Hindu mythology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_mythology "Hindu mythology"), he has been seen as a symbol of hard work, dedication and concentration.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-6)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

Instituted in 1961 to honour the outstanding sportspersons of the country,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-7) the award over the years has undergone a number of expansions, reviews, and rationalizations. The award was expanded to include all the recognised disciplines in 1977, has introduced indigenous games and physically handicapped categories in 1995 and introduced a lifetime contribution category in 1995 leading to creation of a separate [Dhyan Chand Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhyan_Chand_Award "Dhyan Chand Award") in 2002.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-8)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-9) The latest revision in 2018 stipulates that the award is given only to the disciplines included in the events like [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games"), [Paralympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paralympic_Games "Paralympic Games"), [Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Games "Asian Games"), [Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Games "Commonwealth Games"), [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_championship "World championship") and [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_cup_competition "World cup competition") along with [Cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket"), Indigenous Games, and [Parasports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disabled_sports "Disabled sports"). It also recommends giving only fifteen awards in a year, relaxing in case of excellent performance in major [multi-sport events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-sport_event "Multi-sport event"), team sports, across gender and giving at least one award to the physically challenged category.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-Scheme-1)

The nominations for the award are received from all government-recognised National Sports Federations, the [Indian Olympic Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Olympic_Association "Indian Olympic Association"), the [Sports Authority of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Authority_of_India "Sports Authority of India") (SAI), the Sports Promotion and Control Boards, the state and the union territory governments and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, Arjuna, [Dhyan Chand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhyan_Chand_Award "Dhyan Chand Award") and [Dronacharya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dronacharya_Award "Dronacharya Award") awardees of the previous years. The recipients are selected by a committee constituted by the Ministry and are honoured for their "good performance in the field of sports over a period of four years" at international level and for having shown "qualities of leadership, sportsmanship and a sense of discipline".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-Scheme-1)

## Recipients

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Recipients")]

A total of 178 awards were presented in the 2010s: fifteen in 2010, followed by nineteen in 2011, twenty-five in 2012, fourteen in 2013, sixteen in 2014, seventeen in 2015, sixteen in 2016, seventeen in 2017, twenty in 2018 and nineteen in 2019. Individuals from thirty different sports were awarded, including twenty-seven from athletics, sixteen from wrestling, fifteen from shooting, twelve each from cricket and hockey, eleven each from badminton and boxing, nine from kabaddi, eight from archery, six from table tennis, five each from football and swimming, four each from golf, weightlifting and wushu, three each from billiards & snooker, lawn tennis, polo, squash and volleyball, two each from basketball, chess, gymnastics and rowing, and one each from bodybuilding, equestrian, judo, motor sports, roller skating and yachting.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-ArjunaAward-10)

In the initial list of 2013, [triple jumper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_jump "Triple jump")[Renjith Maheshwary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renjith_Maheshwary "Renjith Maheshwary") was mentioned in the discipline of athletics.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-ArjunaAward-10) However, after reports surfaced of him failing a [doping test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doping_in_sport "Doping in sport") in 2008, he was denied the award, making him the first person to be recommended by the Sports Ministry and then denied the award on the day of the function.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-11) Boxer [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar_(boxer) "Manoj Kumar (boxer)"), a gold medalist at the [2010 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Commonwealth_Games "2010 Commonwealth Games") held at [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi"), was initially not on the 2014 awardees list.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-ArjunaAward-10) He filed a case in [Delhi High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_High_Court "Delhi High Court") and the Sports Ministry was directed by the court to present him with the award. The ministry blamed the issue on mistakenly believing him to be involved in a doping case and presented him with the award in November 2014, instead of at the official ceremony at [Rashtrapati Bhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashtrapati_Bhavan "Rashtrapati Bhavan") in August 2014.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-13) Another sportsperson, [para-badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para-badminton "Para-badminton") player [Raj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Kumar_(badminton) "Raj Kumar (badminton)"), a gold medalist in the [2015 Para-Badminton World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Para-Badminton_World_Championships "2015 Para-Badminton World Championships") in England, approached the Delhi High Court after not being awarded the Arjuna Award in 2016. He finally won the legal battle over having higher points than the other para-athlete awarded, and two years later, in September 2018 was given the award for the year 2016.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-15)

[↑](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_ref-a_4-0)The cash prize was introduced in the year 1977–1978 as a scholarship of ₹200 (US$2.10) a month for 2 years.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-16) It was revised to one time cash prize of ₹5,000 (US$52) in 1986,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-17) to ₹20,000 (US$210) in 1987,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-18) to ₹50,000 (US$520) in 1993,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-19) to ₹1.5 lakh (US$1,600) in 1998,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-20) to ₹3 lakh (US$3,100) in 2001,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-21) to ₹5 lakh (US$5,200) in 2009,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-22) and to ₹15 lakh (US$16,000) in 2020.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-23)

The Arjuna Award, officially known as the Arjuna Awards for Outstanding Performance in Sports and Games,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-Scheme-1) is the sports honour of the [Republic of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"). It is awarded annually by the [Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Youth_Affairs_and_Sports "Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports"). Before the introduction of the [Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_Dhyan_Chand_Khel_Ratna "Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna") in 1991–1992, the Arjuna award was the highest sporting honour of India.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-EverestNews-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-3)As of 2020[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)&action=edit), the award comprises "a [bronze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze "Bronze")[statuette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statuette "Statuette") of Arjuna, certificate, ceremonial dress, and a cash prize of ₹15 lakh (US$16,000)."[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-a-4)

## Name

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Name")]

The award is named after [Arjuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjuna "Arjuna"), a character from the [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit") epic _[Mahabharata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahabharata "Mahabharata")_ of [ancient India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_India "History of India"). He is one of the [Pandavas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandavas "Pandavas"), depicted as a skilled [archer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archery "Archery") winning the hand of [Draupadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draupadi "Draupadi") in marriage. In the [Kurukshetra War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurukshetra_War "Kurukshetra War"), Lord [Krishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna "Krishna") becomes his charioteer teaching him the sacred knowledge of [Gita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhagavad_Gita "Bhagavad Gita").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-5) In [Hindu mythology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_mythology "Hindu mythology"), he has been seen as a symbol of hard work, dedication and concentration.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-6)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

Instituted in 1961 to honour the outstanding sportspersons of the country,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-7) the award over the years has undergone a number of expansions, reviews, and rationalizations. The award was expanded to include all the recognised disciplines in 1977, has introduced indigenous games and physically handicapped categories in 1995 and introduced a lifetime contribution category in 1995 leading to creation of a separate [Dhyan Chand Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhyan_Chand_Award "Dhyan Chand Award") in 2002.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-8)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-9) The latest revision in 2018 stipulates that the award is given only to the disciplines included in the events like [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games"), [Paralympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paralympic_Games "Paralympic Games"), [Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Games "Asian Games"), [Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Games "Commonwealth Games"), [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_championship "World championship") and [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_cup_competition "World cup competition") along with [Cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket"), Indigenous Games, and [Parasports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disabled_sports "Disabled sports"). It also recommends giving only fifteen awards in a year, relaxing in case of excellent performance in major [multi-sport events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-sport_event "Multi-sport event"), team sports, across gender and giving at least one award to the physically challenged category.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-Scheme-1)

The nominations for the award are received from all government-recognised National Sports Federations, the [Indian Olympic Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Olympic_Association "Indian Olympic Association"), the [Sports Authority of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Authority_of_India "Sports Authority of India") (SAI), the Sports Promotion and Control Boards, the state and the union territory governments and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, Arjuna, [Dhyan Chand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhyan_Chand_Award "Dhyan Chand Award") and [Dronacharya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dronacharya_Award "Dronacharya Award") awardees of the previous years. The recipients are selected by a committee constituted by the Ministry and are honoured for their "good performance in the field of sports over a period of four years" at international level and for having shown "qualities of leadership, sportsmanship and a sense of discipline".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-Scheme-1)

## Recipients

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Recipients")]

A total of 178 awards were presented in the 2010s: fifteen in 2010, followed by nineteen in 2011, twenty-five in 2012, fourteen in 2013, sixteen in 2014, seventeen in 2015, sixteen in 2016, seventeen in 2017, twenty in 2018 and nineteen in 2019. Individuals from thirty different sports were awarded, including twenty-seven from athletics, sixteen from wrestling, fifteen from shooting, twelve each from cricket and hockey, eleven each from badminton and boxing, nine from kabaddi, eight from archery, six from table tennis, five each from football and swimming, four each from golf, weightlifting and wushu, three each from billiards & snooker, lawn tennis, polo, squash and volleyball, two each from basketball, chess, gymnastics and rowing, and one each from bodybuilding, equestrian, judo, motor sports, roller skating and yachting.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-ArjunaAward-10)

In the initial list of 2013, [triple jumper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_jump "Triple jump")[Renjith Maheshwary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renjith_Maheshwary "Renjith Maheshwary") was mentioned in the discipline of athletics.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-ArjunaAward-10) However, after reports surfaced of him failing a [doping test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doping_in_sport "Doping in sport") in 2008, he was denied the award, making him the first person to be recommended by the Sports Ministry and then denied the award on the day of the function.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-11) Boxer [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar_(boxer) "Manoj Kumar (boxer)"), a gold medalist at the [2010 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Commonwealth_Games "2010 Commonwealth Games") held at [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi"), was initially not on the 2014 awardees list.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-ArjunaAward-10) He filed a case in [Delhi High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_High_Court "Delhi High Court") and the Sports Ministry was directed by the court to present him with the award. The ministry blamed the issue on mistakenly believing him to be involved in a doping case and presented him with the award in November 2014, instead of at the official ceremony at [Rashtrapati Bhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashtrapati_Bhavan "Rashtrapati Bhavan") in August 2014.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-13) Another sportsperson, [para-badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para-badminton "Para-badminton") player [Raj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Kumar_(badminton) "Raj Kumar (badminton)"), a gold medalist in the [2015 Para-Badminton World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Para-Badminton_World_Championships "2015 Para-Badminton World Championships") in England, approached the Delhi High Court after not being awarded the Arjuna Award in 2016. He finally won the legal battle over having higher points than the other para-athlete awarded, and two years later, in September 2018 was given the award for the year 2016.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-15)

## Explanatory notes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Explanatory notes")]

[↑](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_ref-a_4-0)The cash prize was introduced in the year 1977–1978 as a scholarship of ₹200 (US$2.10) a month for 2 years.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-16) It was revised to one time cash prize of ₹5,000 (US$52) in 1986,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-17) to ₹20,000 (US$210) in 1987,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-18) to ₹50,000 (US$520) in 1993,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-19) to ₹1.5 lakh (US$1,600) in 1998,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-20) to ₹3 lakh (US$3,100) in 2001,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-21) to ₹5 lakh (US$5,200) in 2009,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-22) and to ₹15 lakh (US$16,000) in 2020.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Arjuna_Award_recipients_(2010%E2%80%932019)#cite_note-23)

**Abhinav Bindra** (born 28 September 1982) is an Indian former [sport shooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_sports "Shooting sports") and a businessman.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-DOB-1) He is an [Olympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") gold medalist as well as the first and one of only two Indians to win an individual Olympic gold medal.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-rediff_abhinav_wins-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-3) Bindra is also the first Indian to have held concurrently the World and Olympic titles for the men's 10-metre air rifle event, having earned those honours at the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") and the [2006 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_ISSF_World_Shooting_Championships "2006 ISSF World Shooting Championships"). Bindra has won seven medals at the [Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Games "Commonwealth Games") and three medals at the [Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Games "Asian Games").

With more than 150 medals in his 22-year career, he is the recipient of the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") from the Government of India[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-4) and is one of the top influencers of sport policy in the country.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-5)

At the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics") in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), Bindra finished fourth in the finals of the 10-metre air rifle event. He also served as a goodwill ambassador for the Rio 2016 Olympics Indian contingent, having been appointed to that post by the [Indian Olympics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Olympic_Association "Indian Olympic Association") (IOA). On 5 September 2016, he announced his retirement.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-6) Bindra's primary outreach to Indian sports is through the Abhinav Bindra Foundation, a non-profit organisation that works to integrate [sports, science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_science "Sports science"), and technology into Indian sports and encourage high-performance physical training.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-7)

In 2018, Abhinav was bestowed with the prestigious Blue Cross, the [ISSF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Shooting_Sport_Federation "International Shooting Sport Federation")'s highest honour.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-The_blue_cross-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-9) He is also currently a member of the [IOC Athletes' Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOC_Athletes'_Commission "IOC Athletes' Commission").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-10) Bindra carried the [Olympic torch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_torch "Olympic torch") at the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics") in Paris.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-11)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abhinav_Bindra&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abhinav_Bindra&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early years")]

Bindra was born in [Dehradun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehradun "Dehradun") in [Uttarakhand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uttarakhand,_India "Uttarakhand, India"), to a [Punjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabis "Punjabis")[Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh "Sikh")[Khatri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khatri "Khatri") family.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-13) He was educated at [the Doon School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doon_School "The Doon School") in [Dehradun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehradun "Dehradun") and at [St. Stephen's School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Stephen's_School,_Chandigarh "St. Stephen's School, Chandigarh") in [Chandigarh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandigarh "Chandigarh").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-14) He studied [business administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_administration "Business administration") at the [University of Colorado Boulder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Colorado_Boulder "University of Colorado Boulder").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-:0-15) Determined to train with the best possible facilities, which were then not available in India, he would train for prolonged periods in Germany,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-business-16) where he was coached by [Gaby Buhlmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaby_Buhlmann "Gaby Buhlmann").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-historic-solo-17)

### Notable international performances

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abhinav_Bindra&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Notable international performances")]

At the age of 15, Bindra was the youngest participant in the [1998 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_Commonwealth_Games "1998 Commonwealth Games"). He was also the youngest Indian participant at the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") in Sydney. At the 2000 Olympics, he achieved a score of 590, placing him 11th in the qualification round. With that score, he was not able to qualify for the finals. He was also honoured with the Arjuna Award that year.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-18)

In international competitions, he won his first medal, a bronze, at the 2001 Munich World Cup with a new junior world record score of 597/600. He won six gold medals at various international meets that year and received the prestigious [Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_Dhyan_Chand_Khel_Ratna "Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna"), India's highest sports award. In the air rifle event at the [2002 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Commonwealth_Games "2002 Commonwealth Games") in Manchester, he finished with gold in the pairs event and silver in the individual event.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-19)

In the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics") in Athens, he broke the previous Olympic record but did not win a medal. He scored 597 in the qualification round and placed third, preceded by [Qinan Zhu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Qinan "Zhu Qinan") (599, a new Olympic record) and [Li Jie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Jie_(rifle_shooter) "Li Jie (rifle shooter)") (598). In the finals, Abhinav finished with 97.6 points, last in the field of eight; he was the only player with less than 100 points and dropped to the seventh position.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-20)

After these successes, a severe back injury incapacitated him and he was unable to lift a rifle for a year, interrupting his preparation for the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics"). Bindra returned to compete and won the title at the [2006 ISSF World Shooting Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_ISSF_World_Shooting_Championships "2006 ISSF World Shooting Championships") with a score of 699.1, qualifying him for the 2008 Summer Olympics.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-21)

At the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing, Bindra won the men's 10-metre air rifle event, shooting a total of 700.5.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-historic-solo-17) He scored 596 in the qualifying round, finishing fourth, and outscored all other shooters in the finals with a round of 104.5. In the finals, he started with a shot of 10.7, and all others never dipped below 10.0.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-22) Bindra was tied with [Henri Häkkinen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_H%C3%A4kkinen "Henri Häkkinen") heading into his final shot. Bindra scored his highest of the finals – 10.8 – while Hakkinen shot 9.7 to settle for the bronze medal.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-23)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-rediff_abhinav_wins-2)

At the [2010 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Commonwealth_Games "2010 Commonwealth Games") in New Delhi, Bindra was honoured as the national flag-bearer at the opening ceremony. He also was given the honour of taking the athletes' oath on behalf of the 6,700 participants from 71 countries and territories. Bindra, along with [Gagan Narang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gagan_Narang "Gagan Narang"), shot in unison to set a games record of 1,193 points in the 10-metre air rifle pairs event for men to win India's inaugural gold medal at the 19th Commonwealth Games. He brought home a silver medal in the individual event.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-24)

Bindra won the gold medal in the men's 10-metre air rifle event at the 12th [Asian Shooting Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Shooting_Championships "Asian Shooting Championships"), held in [Doha, Qatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doha "Doha").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-25) He lost in the qualification round at the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") in London, finishing in the 16th place with a score of 594. In the [2014 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Commonwealth_Games "2014 Commonwealth Games") in [Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasgow "Glasgow"), Bindra again won gold in the men's 10-metre air rifle singles event.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-26) At the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics") in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), he came fourth in the men's 10-metre air rifle singles event after losing a shoot-off for the top 3 to [Serhiy Kulish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serhiy_Kulish "Serhiy Kulish"), who eventually won the silver medal.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-27)

### Business career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abhinav_Bindra&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Business career")]

Bindra has a bachelor's degree in business administration from the [University of Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Colorado "University of Colorado").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-:0-15) Bindra is the CEO of Abhinav Futuristics Private Limited, an organisation that works to bring science and technology into the sport and healthcare sectors. With ABTP, a group of sports science and advanced physical medicine and rehabilitation (PMR) centres, the organisation has served more than 5,000 athletes and medical patients. Under the Abhinav Bindra Foundation, a non-profit initiative, athletes are provided access to the latest sports technology and high-performance physical training for free.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-business-16) Many athletes from sports such as [swimming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_(sport) "Swimming (sport)"), [badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton "Badminton"), [boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing "Boxing"), and [para-athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para-athletics "Para-athletics") have benefited from the foundation's various programmes. In 2020, he launched the _Abhinav Bindra Sports Medicine and Research Institute at [Bhubaneswar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhubaneswar "Bhubaneswar") with the mission of_ bringing Global Best Practice to the Indian Healthcare and Sports Medicine Sector.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-28)

Since his retirement, Bindra has been involved with the TOP Scheme, one of India's most significant policies for athlete development. He was a member of the ISSF Athlete Committee from 2010 to 2020, serving as [Chair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairperson "Chairperson") from 2014, and was appointed to the IOC Athlete Commission in 2018.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-IOC-ACom-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-30) In these roles he has worked for the development of athletes through mental health, financial stability, and entrepreneurship initiatives. In 2017 whilst Chair of the ISSF Athletes Committee, Bindra was criticised for approving the removal of three events from the Olympic programme in what was described as an undemocratic and un-transparent manner.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-31) Bindra's net worth is estimated to be around $10 million.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-32)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abhinav_Bindra&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Harper Sport published Bindra's autobiography, [_A Shot at History: My Obsessive Journey to Olympic Gold_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Shot_at_History "A Shot at History"), which he co-authored with sportswriter [Rohit Brijnath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rohit_Brijnath "Rohit Brijnath") in October 2011. It was formally released by Union Sports Minister [Ajay Maken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajay_Maken "Ajay Maken") on 27 October 2011, at a function in New Delhi.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-toi-33) The book received positive reviews,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-35) and [Harshvardhan Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harshvardhan_Kapoor "Harshvardhan Kapoor") has been cast for the lead role in a future biopic based on the memoir.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-36)

Abhinav Bindra Coaching

Bindra belongs to a [Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh "Sikh") family and a descendant of legendary warrior [Hari Singh Nalwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hari_Singh_Nalwa "Hari Singh Nalwa"), who was commander-in-chief of the Sikh army during Maharaja [Ranjit Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranjit_Singh "Ranjit Singh")'s reign.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-37)

**Abhinav Bindra** (born 28 September 1982) is an Indian former [sport shooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_sports "Shooting sports") and a businessman.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-DOB-1) He is an [Olympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") gold medalist as well as the first and one of only two Indians to win an individual Olympic gold medal.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-rediff_abhinav_wins-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-3) Bindra is also the first Indian to have held concurrently the World and Olympic titles for the men's 10-metre air rifle event, having earned those honours at the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") and the [2006 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_ISSF_World_Shooting_Championships "2006 ISSF World Shooting Championships"). Bindra has won seven medals at the [Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Games "Commonwealth Games") and three medals at the [Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Games "Asian Games").

With more than 150 medals in his 22-year career, he is the recipient of the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") from the Government of India[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-4) and is one of the top influencers of sport policy in the country.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-5)

At the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics") in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), Bindra finished fourth in the finals of the 10-metre air rifle event. He also served as a goodwill ambassador for the Rio 2016 Olympics Indian contingent, having been appointed to that post by the [Indian Olympics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Olympic_Association "Indian Olympic Association") (IOA). On 5 September 2016, he announced his retirement.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-6) Bindra's primary outreach to Indian sports is through the Abhinav Bindra Foundation, a non-profit organisation that works to integrate [sports, science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_science "Sports science"), and technology into Indian sports and encourage high-performance physical training.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-7)

In 2018, Abhinav was bestowed with the prestigious Blue Cross, the [ISSF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Shooting_Sport_Federation "International Shooting Sport Federation")'s highest honour.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-The_blue_cross-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-9) He is also currently a member of the [IOC Athletes' Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOC_Athletes'_Commission "IOC Athletes' Commission").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-10) Bindra carried the [Olympic torch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_torch "Olympic torch") at the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics") in Paris.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-11)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abhinav_Bindra&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abhinav_Bindra&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early years")]

Bindra was born in [Dehradun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehradun "Dehradun") in [Uttarakhand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uttarakhand,_India "Uttarakhand, India"), to a [Punjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabis "Punjabis")[Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh "Sikh")[Khatri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khatri "Khatri") family.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-13) He was educated at [the Doon School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doon_School "The Doon School") in [Dehradun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehradun "Dehradun") and at [St. Stephen's School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Stephen's_School,_Chandigarh "St. Stephen's School, Chandigarh") in [Chandigarh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandigarh "Chandigarh").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-14) He studied [business administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_administration "Business administration") at the [University of Colorado Boulder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Colorado_Boulder "University of Colorado Boulder").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-:0-15) Determined to train with the best possible facilities, which were then not available in India, he would train for prolonged periods in Germany,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-business-16) where he was coached by [Gaby Buhlmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaby_Buhlmann "Gaby Buhlmann").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-historic-solo-17)

### Notable international performances

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abhinav_Bindra&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Notable international performances")]

At the age of 15, Bindra was the youngest participant in the [1998 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_Commonwealth_Games "1998 Commonwealth Games"). He was also the youngest Indian participant at the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") in Sydney. At the 2000 Olympics, he achieved a score of 590, placing him 11th in the qualification round. With that score, he was not able to qualify for the finals. He was also honoured with the Arjuna Award that year.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-18)

In international competitions, he won his first medal, a bronze, at the 2001 Munich World Cup with a new junior world record score of 597/600. He won six gold medals at various international meets that year and received the prestigious [Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_Dhyan_Chand_Khel_Ratna "Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna"), India's highest sports award. In the air rifle event at the [2002 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Commonwealth_Games "2002 Commonwealth Games") in Manchester, he finished with gold in the pairs event and silver in the individual event.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-19)

In the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics") in Athens, he broke the previous Olympic record but did not win a medal. He scored 597 in the qualification round and placed third, preceded by [Qinan Zhu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Qinan "Zhu Qinan") (599, a new Olympic record) and [Li Jie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Jie_(rifle_shooter) "Li Jie (rifle shooter)") (598). In the finals, Abhinav finished with 97.6 points, last in the field of eight; he was the only player with less than 100 points and dropped to the seventh position.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-20)

After these successes, a severe back injury incapacitated him and he was unable to lift a rifle for a year, interrupting his preparation for the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics"). Bindra returned to compete and won the title at the [2006 ISSF World Shooting Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_ISSF_World_Shooting_Championships "2006 ISSF World Shooting Championships") with a score of 699.1, qualifying him for the 2008 Summer Olympics.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-21)

At the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing, Bindra won the men's 10-metre air rifle event, shooting a total of 700.5.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-historic-solo-17) He scored 596 in the qualifying round, finishing fourth, and outscored all other shooters in the finals with a round of 104.5. In the finals, he started with a shot of 10.7, and all others never dipped below 10.0.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-22) Bindra was tied with [Henri Häkkinen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_H%C3%A4kkinen "Henri Häkkinen") heading into his final shot. Bindra scored his highest of the finals – 10.8 – while Hakkinen shot 9.7 to settle for the bronze medal.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-23)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-rediff_abhinav_wins-2)

At the [2010 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Commonwealth_Games "2010 Commonwealth Games") in New Delhi, Bindra was honoured as the national flag-bearer at the opening ceremony. He also was given the honour of taking the athletes' oath on behalf of the 6,700 participants from 71 countries and territories. Bindra, along with [Gagan Narang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gagan_Narang "Gagan Narang"), shot in unison to set a games record of 1,193 points in the 10-metre air rifle pairs event for men to win India's inaugural gold medal at the 19th Commonwealth Games. He brought home a silver medal in the individual event.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-24)

Bindra won the gold medal in the men's 10-metre air rifle event at the 12th [Asian Shooting Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Shooting_Championships "Asian Shooting Championships"), held in [Doha, Qatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doha "Doha").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-25) He lost in the qualification round at the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") in London, finishing in the 16th place with a score of 594. In the [2014 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Commonwealth_Games "2014 Commonwealth Games") in [Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasgow "Glasgow"), Bindra again won gold in the men's 10-metre air rifle singles event.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-26) At the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics") in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), he came fourth in the men's 10-metre air rifle singles event after losing a shoot-off for the top 3 to [Serhiy Kulish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serhiy_Kulish "Serhiy Kulish"), who eventually won the silver medal.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-27)

### Business career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abhinav_Bindra&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Business career")]

Bindra has a bachelor's degree in business administration from the [University of Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Colorado "University of Colorado").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-:0-15) Bindra is the CEO of Abhinav Futuristics Private Limited, an organisation that works to bring science and technology into the sport and healthcare sectors. With ABTP, a group of sports science and advanced physical medicine and rehabilitation (PMR) centres, the organisation has served more than 5,000 athletes and medical patients. Under the Abhinav Bindra Foundation, a non-profit initiative, athletes are provided access to the latest sports technology and high-performance physical training for free.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-business-16) Many athletes from sports such as [swimming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_(sport) "Swimming (sport)"), [badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton "Badminton"), [boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing "Boxing"), and [para-athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para-athletics "Para-athletics") have benefited from the foundation's various programmes. In 2020, he launched the _Abhinav Bindra Sports Medicine and Research Institute at [Bhubaneswar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhubaneswar "Bhubaneswar") with the mission of_ bringing Global Best Practice to the Indian Healthcare and Sports Medicine Sector.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-28)

Since his retirement, Bindra has been involved with the TOP Scheme, one of India's most significant policies for athlete development. He was a member of the ISSF Athlete Committee from 2010 to 2020, serving as [Chair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairperson "Chairperson") from 2014, and was appointed to the IOC Athlete Commission in 2018.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-IOC-ACom-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-30) In these roles he has worked for the development of athletes through mental health, financial stability, and entrepreneurship initiatives. In 2017 whilst Chair of the ISSF Athletes Committee, Bindra was criticised for approving the removal of three events from the Olympic programme in what was described as an undemocratic and un-transparent manner.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-31) Bindra's net worth is estimated to be around $10 million.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-32)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Abhinav_Bindra&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Harper Sport published Bindra's autobiography, [_A Shot at History: My Obsessive Journey to Olympic Gold_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Shot_at_History "A Shot at History"), which he co-authored with sportswriter [Rohit Brijnath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rohit_Brijnath "Rohit Brijnath") in October 2011. It was formally released by Union Sports Minister [Ajay Maken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajay_Maken "Ajay Maken") on 27 October 2011, at a function in New Delhi.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-toi-33) The book received positive reviews,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-35) and [Harshvardhan Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harshvardhan_Kapoor "Harshvardhan Kapoor") has been cast for the lead role in a future biopic based on the memoir.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-36)

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/Abhinav_Bindra_Coaching.png/250px-Abhinav_Bindra_Coaching.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Abhinav_Bindra_Coaching.png)

Abhinav Bindra Coaching

Bindra belongs to a [Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh "Sikh") family and a descendant of legendary warrior [Hari Singh Nalwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hari_Singh_Nalwa "Hari Singh Nalwa"), who was commander-in-chief of the Sikh army during Maharaja [Ranjit Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranjit_Singh "Ranjit Singh")'s reign.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhinav_Bindra#cite_note-37)

**Krishna Poonia** (born 5 May 1977) is an Indian [politician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politician "Politician") and former [discus thrower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discus_throw "Discus throw"). A former [Commonwealth Games Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2010_Commonwealth_Games_%E2%80%93_Women's_discus_throw "Athletics at the 2010 Commonwealth Games – Women's discus throw"), she represented India in the women's discus throw event at the [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") and [2012 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics"). In recognition of her contributions to Indian athletics, she received the Arjuna Award in 2010 and the [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") in 2011. Poonia later entered politics and served as a [Member of the Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_Legislative_Assembly_(India) "Member of the Legislative Assembly (India)") from the [Sadulpur constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadulpur_Assembly_constituency "Sadulpur Assembly constituency"), representing the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress") in 2018.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-bidhwanpoonia2-2)

## Early and personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krishna_Poonia&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early and personal life")]

Krishna was born on 5 May 1977 in [Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu "Hindu")[Jat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jat "Jat") family of [Agroha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agroha_(town) "Agroha (town)") in [Haryana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haryana "Haryana").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-3) Her ancestral place was [Bidhwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bidhwan "Bidhwan") village of [Siwani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siwani "Siwani") block of [Bhiwani district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhiwani_district "Bhiwani district"), her family migrated to Agroha[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-4) where she was born. She was raised by her father and paternal grandmother after her mother died when she was nine years old.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-jatni1-5) Her physical fitness was honed as a result of working at her family land since the age of 15 and not exactly undergoing rigorous sports training.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-Matthew_Knight_and_Olivia_Yasukawa-6) Krishna obtained a [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") degree in [sociology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociology "Sociology") from [Fateh Chand College for Women, Hisar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fateh_Chand_College_for_Women_(Lahore),_Hisar "Fateh Chand College for Women (Lahore), Hisar").

In 2000, she married Virender Singh Poonia, a former athlete who coached her after their marriage, and had a son in 2001.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-jatni1-5) The couple worked for [Indian Railways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Railways "Indian Railways") but in 2013, Poonia resigned and joined the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krishna_Poonia&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 2010 Commonwealth Games

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krishna_Poonia&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2010 Commonwealth Games")]

Poonia became the first Indian woman athlete to win a gold medal at the [2010 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Commonwealth_Games "2010 Commonwealth Games") in Delhi. Poonia led the historic clean sweep of the discus event by clearing 61.51 m. She is the first Indian woman to win a gold medal in track and field events of Commonwealth Games and the first Indian to win a gold medal in such events after [Milkha Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milkha_Singh "Milkha Singh") who had won the gold in men's 440 yards race in the [1958 Cardiff Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_British_Empire_and_Commonwealth_Games "1958 British Empire and Commonwealth Games").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-CWGgold-9)

### 2012 London Olympics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krishna_Poonia&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2012 London Olympics")]

She finished a creditable sixth in the women's discus throw in the 2012 London Olympics. Poonia's best effort of 63.62 m came in her fifth and penultimate attempt. She had 62.42 m in the first attempt and 61.61 in the third and 61.31 m in the sixth and the final throw. She had two no-throws in the second and the fourth attempt. Earlier she became only the sixth Indian to make it to the final round of an Olympic track and field event after [Milkha Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milkha_Singh "Milkha Singh"), [P T Usha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P_T_Usha "P T Usha"), [Sriram Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriram_Singh "Sriram Singh"), [Gurbachan Singh Randhawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gurbachan_Singh_Randhawa "Gurbachan Singh Randhawa") and [Anju Bobby George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anju_Bobby_George "Anju Bobby George").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-11)

## Political career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Krishna_Poonia&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Political career")]

In 2013, she joined the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress") at an election rally in Churu – her husband's home district – in the presence of [Rahul Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahul_Gandhi "Rahul Gandhi") and then chief minister [Ashok Gehlot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashok_Gehlot "Ashok Gehlot") after she was approached by the Congress's leadership.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-bidhwanpoonia2-2)

In [2013 Rajasthan Legislative Assembly election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Rajasthan_Legislative_Assembly_election "2013 Rajasthan Legislative Assembly election"), she contested and lost her first election from the [Sadulpur Assembly constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadulpur_(Rajasthan_Assembly_constituency) "Sadulpur (Rajasthan Assembly constituency)") as Congress candidate where she finished third behind [BJP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") and [BSP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahujan_Samaj_Party "Bahujan Samaj Party").

In [2018 Rajasthan Legislative Assembly election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Rajasthan_Legislative_Assembly_election "2018 Rajasthan Legislative Assembly election"), she contested again and won the same seat on a Congress ticket, by a margin of 18,084 votes.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-bidhwanpoonia1-12)

In [2019 Lok Sabha Elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Indian_general_election "2019 Indian general election"), Poonia was nominated by Congress from the [Jaipur Rural constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur_Rural_Lok_Sabha_constituency "Jaipur Rural Lok Sabha constituency"). She contested against Olympian [Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajyavardhan_Singh_Rathore "Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore") of the [BJP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-13) She lost to Rathore by a margin of 3,93,171 votes.

Poonia has been helping Rajasthan State Health Ministry in its attempt to curb female foeticide as the selective abortion of female fetuses is a pressing concern in India especially in Haryana where Poonia grew up. She is also engaged in improving the infrastructure of sports for children in Jaipur and across the country.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-Matthew_Knight_and_Olivia_Yasukawa-6)

She was appointed as the president of Rajasthan State Sports Council in 2022.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-14)

In [2023 Rajasthan Legislative Assembly election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Rajasthan_Legislative_Assembly_election "2023 Rajasthan Legislative Assembly election"), she lost the election from the [Sadulpur Assembly constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadulpur_Assembly_constituency "Sadulpur Assembly constituency") as Congress candidate by a margin of 2,574 votes behind [BSP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahujan_Samaj_Party "Bahujan Samaj Party").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_Poonia#cite_note-15)
